label: United Kingdom (MHRA): UK-wide marketing authorisations
summary: MHRA classifies variations with the EU guidelines of 2013 (2013/C 223/01) until it issues its own, so since the EU moved to its 2025 guidelines on 15 January 2026 the same change can fall in a different category in the UK and the EU. Since 1 January 2025 marketing authorisations granted by MHRA are UK-wide (Windsor Framework). Variations go to MHRA directly, or through the International Recognition Procedure when a reference regulator has approved the same change.

categories.label: No variation needed
categories.rule: No submission: the change is managed under the quality system (or an approved protocol).

categories.label: Separate procedure (not a variation)
categories.rule: Use the procedure named in the result (for example a transfer or an Article 61(3) notification).

categories.label: Type IA
categories.rule: Implement, then notify within 12 months (for example in the Type IA annual update). MHRA checks it within 30 days.

categories.label: Type IA-IN
categories.rule: Implement, then notify immediately. MHRA checks it within 30 days.

categories.label: Type IB
categories.rule: Notify before implementing; if MHRA raises no objection within 30 days of a valid notification, the change is accepted.

categories.label: Type II
categories.rule: Implement only after approval: quality-only changes once the opinion or outcome is received; changes to the product information once the decision is amended.

categories.label: Extension application
categories.rule: An extension is assessed like a new application and needs a decision before marketing.

13:B.II.b.1:1.text: Satisfactory inspection in the last three years.

13:B.II.b.1:2.text: The site is authorised for the pharmaceutical form or product.

13:B.II.b.1:4.text: Validation done at the new site where relevant.

13:B.II.b.1:5.text: The product is not biological or immunological.

13:B.II.b.2:3.text: The product is not biological or immunological.

13:B.II.b.2:5.text: At least one testing site stays in the UK or an MRA country.

13:B.II.b.3:1.text: No change in impurity profile or physicochemical properties.

13:B.II.b.3:2.text: Immediate-release solid oral form or oral solution (not biological or herbal), or a parameter already judged to have no quality impact.

13:B.II.b.3:3.text: Same manufacturing principle and steps, no solvent change.

13:B.II.b.3:4.text: Process controlled by existing in-process controls, with no limit changes.

13:B.II.b.3:6.text: The product is identical in quality, safety and efficacy.

13:B.II.b.3:7.text: Stability studies started, with at least three months of data.

13:B.II.b.4:2.text: Conventional immediate-release oral form or non-sterile liquid.

13:B.II.b.4:3.text: Method changes only those the new size needs.

13:B.II.b.4:4.text: Validation on three batches of the new size, or a validation scheme.

13:B.II.b.4:5.text: Not a biological or immunological product.

13:B.II.b.4:6.text: Not caused by unexpected events or stability concerns.

13:B.II.b.4:7.text: Within ten times the originally approved size.

13:B.II.b.5:1.text: Not required by an earlier commitment.

13:B.II.b.5:2.text: Not caused by unexpected manufacturing events.

13:B.II.b.5:5.text: The new method is not novel or non-standard.

13:B.II.b.5:6.text: The new method is not biological or immunological.

13:B.II.b.5:7.text: The test does not control a critical parameter.

13:B.I.a.1:1.text: Same specifications, methods and route as approved.

13:B.I.a.1:2.text: The active substance is neither biological nor sterile.

13:B.I.a.1:3.text: No new supplier of materials of human or animal origin needing TSE or viral assessment.

13:B.I.a.2:1.text: No adverse change in impurity profile or physicochemical properties.

13:B.I.a.2:2.text: Same route, no new reagents, catalysts or solvents.

13:B.II.a.1:4.text: Markings that tell strengths apart are not removed.

13:B.II.a.3:2.text: Weight adjustment via an excipient that is a major part of the formulation.

13:B.II.a.3:4.text: Stability studies started, at least three months of data.

13:B.II.a.3:8.text: Comparable dissolution on two pilot batches.

13:B.II.d.1:1.text: Not required by an earlier commitment to review limits.

13:B.II.d.1:2.text: Not caused by unexpected manufacturing events.

13:B.II.d.1:4.text: Test procedure unchanged or only minor changes.

13:B.II.d.1:5.text: The new method is not novel.

13:B.II.d.1:6.text: The method is not biological or immunological.

13:B.II.d.1:7.text: The change does not concern impurities (including genotoxic) or dissolution.

13:B.II.d.2:1.text: Validation shows the updated procedure is at least equivalent.

13:B.II.d.2:2.text: Total impurity limits unchanged, no new unqualified impurities.

13:B.II.d.2:3.text: Method of analysis stays the same.

13:B.II.d.2:4.text: The method is not biological or immunological.

13:B.II.e.1:3.text: Stability studies started with relevant data.

13:B.II.e.4:1.text: No change in the composition of the container.

13:B.II.e.4:2.text: Not a fundamental part of the packaging.

13:B.II.e.4:3.text: Stability studies if headspace or surface-to-volume ratio changes.

13:B.II.e.5:1.text: Pack size consistent with the posology and treatment duration.

13:B.II.e.6:1.text: No effect on delivery, use, safety or stability.

13:B.II.f.1:1.text: The change is not the result of unexpected events during manufacture or of stability concerns.

13:B.II.f.1:2.text: No widening of criteria, no removal of stability-indicating parameters, no reduced testing.

13:A.7:1.text: At least one site that performs the same function remains authorised.

13:A.7:2.text: The deletion is not caused by critical deficiencies in manufacture.

13:A.5:1.text: The site and all its manufacturing operations stay the same.

13:A.3:1.text: The active substance itself stays the same.

13:B.II.b.2:6.text: The batch release site is in the UK (or the arrangements MHRA accepts for release), and at least one testing site stays in the UK or an MRA country.

13:B.III.1:1.text: Release and end-of-shelf-life specifications of the finished product stay the same.

13:B.III.1:2.text: Additional product-specific specifications for impurities and other requirements stay the same (apart from tightening).

13:B.III.1:3.text: The active substance is tested immediately before use if no re-test period is in the certificate.

13:B.III.1:4.text: No materials of human or animal origin that need a viral safety assessment are used.

13:B.I.a.3:1.text: The increase is up to 10 times the batch size approved when the marketing authorisation was granted (or a decrease of up to 10 times).

13:B.I.a.3:2.text: The change is only to scale-related equipment and does not affect the reproducibility of the process.

13:B.I.a.3:3.text: The change is not the result of unexpected events during manufacture or stability concerns.

13:B.I.a.3:4.text: The active substance is not biological or immunological.

13:B.II.a.4:1.text: The dissolution profile of the new product is comparable to the old one.

13:B.II.a.4:2.text: The coating is not critical to the release mechanism.

13:B.II.a.4:3.text: The finished product specification changes only in weight and dimensions, if at all.

13:B.II.a.2:1.text: The dissolution profile of the reshaped product is comparable to the old one.

13:B.II.a.2:2.text: Release and end-of-shelf-life specifications are unchanged apart from dimensions.

13:B.II.a.2:3.text: The qualitative and quantitative composition and mean mass are unchanged.

13:B.II.c.3:1.text: Release and end-of-shelf-life specifications of the excipient and the finished product are unchanged.

13:B.II.c.1:1.text: The change is not the result of a commitment from an earlier assessment or of unexpected events during manufacture.

13:B.II.c.1:2.text: The new test method is not novel or non-standard.

13:B.II.c.1:3.text: The deleted test is non-significant or obsolete.

13:B.II.e.7:1.text: The qualitative and quantitative composition of the packaging component is unchanged.

13:B.II.e.7:2.text: The specifications and quality control are at least equivalent.

13:B.II.e.7:3.text: Any sterilisation method and conditions are unchanged.

13:B.II.e.7:4.text: It is not a spacer device for a metered-dose inhaler.

13:B.I.d.1:1.text: The change is not the result of unexpected events during manufacture or of stability concerns.

13:A.2:1.text: MHRA has finished checking the new name and found it acceptable.

13:B.II.b.5:8.text: The new analytical procedure is validated and at least equivalent to the old one.

13:B.I.b.2:1.text: Validation shows the new procedure is at least equivalent to the old one.

13:B.I.b.2:2.text: The method of analysis stays the same (for example a change in column length, not a new technique).

13:B.IV.1:1.text: The device is CE or UKCA marked as a medical device.

13:B.IV.1:2.text: The delivered dose is accurate and compatible with the posology.

multipleChanges.rule: Several variations can be grouped in one submission when they are related or MHRA agrees; a group follows the procedure of its highest type. Type IA changes can be collected in an annual update.

IA.label: Notify within 12 months of implementation (annual update)

IB.label: Accepted if no objection within 30 days of a valid notification

II.label: 60-day assessment (90 days for changes to indications, 30 for some urgent safety changes), plus clock stops

EXT.label: Assessed like an initial application: 210 days plus clock stops, then the decision

variation.label: Cover letter listing the variations, their classification and the route (national or International Recognition Procedure)
Variation application form submitted through the MHRA portal, with the present/proposed table and the declaration of conditions met

pi.label: Product information (SmPC, labelling, package leaflet), clean and with changes highlighted

irp.label: International Recognition Procedure: reference regulator’s approval decision (and assessment report where available)

other.label: Cover letter or notification for the procedure named in the result

changeLog.text: First UK edition: all 120 changes classified with the 2013 guidelines as MHRA still applies them, with UK sources and wording, the UK-wide marketing authorisation and the International Recognition Procedure for variations.
